sentences.zh: =韋溫=

translations.literal: =Wei Wen=
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen

sentences.zh: 韋溫，字弘育，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Wen, styled Hongyu, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen, courtesy name Hongyu, came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖肇，吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao had served as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父綬，德宗朝翰林學士，以散騎常侍致仕。

translations.literal: His father Shou was a Hanlin Academician in the Dezong reign and retired as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shou had been a Hanlin Academician under Emperor Dezong and retired with the title of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 綬弟貫之，憲宗朝宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother Guanzhi was a chief minister in the Xianzong reign and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Guanzhi had served as chief minister under Emperor Xianzong and is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 溫七歲時，日念《毛詩》一卷。

translations.literal: When Wen was seven, he recited one fascicle of the Mao Odes each day.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven, Wen could recite one fascicle of the Mao Odes every day.

sentences.zh: 年十一歲，應兩經舉登第。

translations.literal: At eleven he entered the examinations for the two Classics and passed.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he took the examinations in the two Classics and passed.

sentences.zh: 釋褐太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: On leaving the boll he was appointed Ceremonial Attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On completing his studies he was appointed Ceremonial Attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以書判拔萃，調補秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Through outstanding performance in the document-judgment examination he was transferred and appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After distinguishing himself in the document-judgment examination, he was posted as Proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時綬致仕田園，聞溫登第，愕然曰：「判入高等，在群士之上，得非交結權幸而致耶？

translations.literal: At that time Shou had retired to his estate; hearing that Wen had passed, he said in astonishment, "To rank in the highest grade, above the mass of candidates—could this not have been achieved by currying favor with the powerful?"
translations.idiomatic: Shou had by then retired to his country estate. When he heard that Wen had passed the examination, he exclaimed in surprise, "To place in the highest grade, above all the other candidates—surely this was not won by cultivating connections with the powerful?"

sentences.zh: 」令設席於廷，自出判目試兩節。

translations.literal: " He had a seat set up in the courtyard and himself produced judgment topics to test him on two sections.
translations.idiomatic: " He set out a seat in the courtyard and himself drew up judgment topics to test Wen on two sections.

sentences.zh: 溫命筆即成，綬喜曰：「此無愧也！

translations.literal: Wen took up the brush and finished at once; Shou said with delight, "This is without shame!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen took up his brush and completed the exercise at once. Shou said with delight, "There is nothing here to be ashamed of!"

sentences.zh: 」調授咸陽尉。

translations.literal: " He was transferred and appointed magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen was then appointed magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，以父在田裏，憲府禮拘，難於省謁，不拜。

translations.literal: He entered service as Investigating Censor; because his father was in the countryside and the censorate's ritual constraints made visiting difficult, he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor, but because his father was living in the countryside and the censorate's ritual restrictions made it difficult to visit him, he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 換著作郎，一謝即還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Archivist; after one audience he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Archivist, paid one visit of thanks at court, and then returned home.

sentences.zh: 侍省父疾，溫侍醫藥，衣不解帶，垂二十年。

translations.literal: He attended his father in illness; Wen served him with medicine, never loosening his belt, for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, Wen nursed him, attending to his medicine and never removing his belt at night, for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 父憂，毀瘠逾制。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he wasted away beyond the prescribed measure.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he grieved himself into emaciation beyond what ritual required.

sentences.zh: 免喪，久之為右補闕，忠鯁救時。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, after some time he became Right Remonstrator, loyal and upright in saving the age.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he eventually became Right Remonstrator, serving with loyal forthrightness to remedy the times.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫被誣，溫倡言曰：「宋公履行有素，身居臺輔，不當有此，是奸人陷害也。

translations.literal: When Song Shenxi was slandered, Wen took the lead in saying, "Lord Song's conduct has long been consistent; holding office at the highest level, he ought not to have this—it is the work of villains framing him."
translations.idiomatic: When Song Shenxi was falsely accused, Wen spoke out first: "Lord Song's conduct has always been upright. As a chief minister he should not be subject to such charges—this is a frame-up by schemers."

sentences.zh: 吾輩諫官，豈避一時之雷電，而致聖君賢相蒙蔽惑之咎耶？

translations.literal: We remonstrating officials—how can we shrink from a moment's thunder and lightning and thereby incur the blame of letting our sage ruler and worthy chancellor be deceived and misled?"
translations.idiomatic: Are we remonstrating officials to shrink from a moment's wrath and thereby bear the guilt of letting our sage ruler and worthy chancellor be deceived?"

sentences.zh: 」因率同列伏閣切爭之，由是知名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his colleagues in prostrating themselves at the gate and arguing urgently, and by this became well known.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his colleagues in kneeling at the palace gate and pressing their remonstrance, and by this act won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，太廟第四、第六室缺漏，上怒，罰宗正卿李銳、將作王堪，乃詔中使鳩工補葺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, the fourth and sixth chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were damaged; the emperor was angry, punished Director of the Imperial Clan Li Rui and Director of Palace Construction Wang Kan, and ordered eunuch commissioners to gather workers to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Taihe era, the fourth and sixth chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were found damaged. The emperor was enraged, penalized Director of the Imperial Clan Li Rui and Director of Palace Construction Wang Kan, and ordered eunuch commissioners to gather workmen to make repairs.

sentences.zh: 溫上疏曰：「臣聞吏舉其職，國家所以治；

translations.literal: Wen submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that when officials perform their duties, the state is thereby governed;
translations.idiomatic: Wen submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that when officials perform their proper duties, the state is governed;

sentences.zh: 事歸於正，朝廷所以尊。

translations.literal: when affairs return to what is correct, the court is thereby honored.
translations.idiomatic: when affairs are handled as they should be, the court is thereby honored.

sentences.zh: 夫設制度，立官司，事存典故，國有經費，而最重者，奉宗廟也。

translations.literal: In establishing institutions, setting up offices, preserving precedents, and maintaining state expenditures, nothing is weightier than serving the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing institutions, creating offices, preserving precedents, and allocating state funds, nothing is more weighty than the service of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 伏以太廟當修，詔下逾月，有司弛墮，曾不加誡。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that when the Imperial Temple required repair, more than a month passed after the edict was issued and the responsible offices were negligent, yet no reprimand was added.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Temple required repair, more than a month passed after the edict was issued while the responsible offices remained negligent, yet no additional reprimand was imposed.

sentences.zh: 宜黜慢官，以懲不恪之罪；

translations.literal: Negligent officials should be dismissed to punish the crime of inattention;
translations.idiomatic: Negligent officials should be removed to punish their lack of diligence;

sentences.zh: 擇可任者，責以繕完之功。

translations.literal: capable men should be chosen and charged with the work of complete repair.
translations.idiomatic: capable men should be selected and charged with completing the repairs.

sentences.zh: 此則事歸於正，吏舉其職也。

translations.literal: Then affairs would return to what is correct and officials would perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In this way affairs would be handled properly and officials would perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 而聖思不勞，百職無曠。

translations.literal: The sage mind would not be troubled and no office would stand vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's mind would not be burdened and no office would be left neglected.

sentences.zh: 今慢官不恪，止於罰俸，宗廟所切，便委內臣，是許百司之官，公然廢職，以宗廟之重，為陛下所私，群官有司，便同委棄。

translations.literal: Now negligent officials who were inattentive received only salary penalties; what the ancestral temple urgently required was entrusted to inner attendants—this permits officials of all bureaus openly to abandon their duties, treats the weight of the ancestral temple as Your Majesty's private concern, and casts aside the assembled officials and responsible offices as one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now negligent officials received only salary penalties, while what the ancestral temple urgently required was entrusted to inner attendants. This permits officials throughout the government openly to abandon their duties, treats the weight of the ancestral temple as Your Majesty's private affair, and effectively casts aside the assembled officials and responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 此臣竊為聖朝惜此事也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately grieves for the sage court in this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately grieves that the sage court should suffer this.

sentences.zh: 事關宗廟，皆書史策，茍非舊典，不可率然。

translations.literal: Matters touching the ancestral temple are all recorded in the histories; if they are not ancient precedent, they cannot be undertaken rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Matters touching the ancestral temple are all recorded in the histories; if they are not established precedent, they cannot be undertaken lightly.

sentences.zh: 伏乞更下詔書，得委所司營繕，則制度不紊，官業交修。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly begs that another edict be issued entrusting the work to the proper offices for construction and repair; then institutions would not be disordered and official duties would be jointly fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly begs that another edict be issued entrusting the repairs to the proper offices, so that institutions would not be disordered and official duties would be properly performed.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止內使。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon stopped the inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon recalled the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 群臣上尊號，溫上疏曰：「德如三皇止稱皇，功如五帝止稱帝。

translations.literal: When the assembled ministers proposed an honorific title, Wen submitted a memorial saying, "If virtue is like the Three Sovereigns, one is called only Huang; if merit is like the Five Emperors, one is called only Di."
translations.idiomatic: When the assembled ministers proposed an honorific title, Wen submitted a memorial: "If one's virtue equals the Three Sovereigns, one is called only Huang; if one's merit equals the Five Emperors, one is called only Di."

sentences.zh: 徽號之來，乃聖王之末事。

translations.literal: The coming of honorific epithets is the last affair of sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Honorific epithets belong to the last resort of sage kings.

sentences.zh: 今歲三川水災，江淮旱歉，恐非崇飾徽稱之時。

translations.literal: This year the Three Rivers have suffered flood, and the Huai and Yangzi regions drought and poor harvest—this is perhaps not the time to exalt and adorn with honorific titles.
translations.idiomatic: This year the Three Rivers have flooded, and the Huai and Yangzi regions have suffered drought and poor harvests—this is scarcely the time to exalt oneself with honorific titles.

sentences.zh: 」帝深嘉之，乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly praised this and stopped the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor greatly approved and abandoned the proposal.

sentences.zh: 改侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 李德裕作相，遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu became chief minister, Wen was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu became chief minister, Wen was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 或以溫厚於牛僧孺，言於德裕。

translations.literal: Some, because Wen was close to Niu Sengru, spoke of this to Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Some people, noting Wen's closeness to Niu Sengru, mentioned this to Deyu.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「此人堅正中立，君子也。

translations.literal: Deyu said, "This man is firm, upright, and impartial—a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "This man is firm, upright, and impartial—a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」鄭註鎮鳳翔，自知不為所齒，求德門弟子為參佐，請溫為副使。

translations.literal: " Zheng Zhu was stationed at Fengxiang; knowing he was not regarded as an equal, he sought a disciple of the Virtue Gate as aide and requested Wen as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Zhu was posted to Fengxiang. Knowing he was not regarded as an equal by men of standing, he sought a disciple of the Virtue Gate as an aide and requested Wen as his deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 或以為理不可拒，拒則生患。

translations.literal: Some held that by reason it could not be refused, and that refusal would breed trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that reason forbade refusal and that to refuse would invite trouble.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「擇禍莫若輕。

translations.literal: Wen said, "In choosing calamity, none is lighter than the other."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "When choosing between calamities, take the lighter one."

sentences.zh: 拒之止於遠貶，從之有不測之禍。

translations.literal: Refusal would end only in distant demotion; compliance would bring unforeseeable disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Refusal would at worst mean distant demotion; compliance could bring unforeseeable disaster.

sentences.zh: 」鄭註誅，轉考功員外郎。

translations.literal: " After Zheng Zhu was executed, Wen was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's merit section.
translations.idiomatic: " After Zheng Zhu was executed, Wen was transferred to Vice Director in the merit section of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋知制誥，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Drafting Secretary and summoned into the Hanlin as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Drafting Secretary and summoned into the Hanlin Academy as Academician.

sentences.zh: 以父職禁廷，憂畏成病，遺誡不令居禁職，懇辭不拜。

translations.literal: Because his father had served in the forbidden precincts of the court, he was gripped by worry and fear until he fell ill; his father's dying injunction forbade him to hold a forbidden post, and he earnestly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had served within the forbidden precincts of the court, Wen was consumed by worry and fear until he fell ill. His father's dying injunction forbade him from holding such a post, and he earnestly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子侍讀，每晨至少陽院，午見莊恪太子。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Reader-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent; each morning he went to the Shaoyang Court and at noon saw Heir Apparent Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Reader-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent. Each morning he went to the Shaoyang Court, and at noon he attended upon Heir Apparent Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「殿下盛年，宜早起，學周文王為太子，雞鳴時問安西宮。

translations.literal: Wen said, "Your Highness is in the prime of youth and ought to rise early, emulating King Wen of Zhou as heir, who at cockcrow inquired after the empress dowager in the Western Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "Your Highness is in the prime of youth and ought to rise early, following the example of King Wen of Zhou as crown prince, who at cockcrow went to inquire after the empress dowager in the Western Palace."

sentences.zh: 」太子幼，不能行其言。

translations.literal: " The heir was young and could not act on his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The heir was young and could not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 稱疾。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wen pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 王晏平為靈武，刻削軍士，贓罪發，帝以智興之故，減死，貶官。

translations.literal: Wang Yanping was at Lingwu and extorted the soldiers; when his corruption was exposed, the emperor, because of Zhixing, reduced the sentence from death and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanping, posted to Lingwu, had extorted his soldiers. When his corruption was exposed, the emperor, out of regard for Zhixing, commuted the death sentence and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 溫三封詔書，文宗深獎之。

translations.literal: Wen three times sealed back the edict; Emperor Wenzong greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen three times returned the edict unapproved, and Emperor Wenzong greatly commended him.

sentences.zh: 莊恪得罪，召百僚諭之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangke fell from favor, the emperor summoned the hundred officials to explain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangke fell from favor, the emperor summoned the officials to explain the matter.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「太子年幼，陛下訓之不早，到此非獨太子之過。

translations.literal: Wen said, "The heir is young; Your Majesty did not instruct him early—reaching this point is not the heir's fault alone."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The heir is young. Your Majesty did not instruct him early enough—what has happened is not the heir's fault alone."

sentences.zh: 」遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部員外郎張文規父弘靖，長慶初在幽州為硃克融所囚；

translations.literal: Zhang Wengui, Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, had a father Hongjing who in the early Changqing era was imprisoned at Youzhou by Zhu Kerong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wengui, Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, had a father named Hongjing who in the early Changqing era had been imprisoned at Youzhou by Zhu Kerong;

sentences.zh: 文規不時省赴，人士喧然罪之。

translations.literal: Wengui did not promptly go to visit him, and gentlemen loudly condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui had not promptly gone to visit him, and men of standing loudly condemned him.

sentences.zh: 溫居綱轄，首糾其事，出文規為安州刺史。

translations.literal: Wen held the reins of office and was first to impeach him in this matter, sending Wengui out as prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, holding authority in personnel matters, was the first to impeach him and had Wengui sent out as prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵判官姚勖知河陰院，嘗雪冤獄。

translations.literal: Salt and Iron Commission assessor Yao Xu supervised the Heyin depot and once cleared a wrongful case.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xu, assessor of the Salt and Iron Commission, supervised the Heyin depot and had once cleared a wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使崔珙奏加酬獎，乃令權知職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Salt and Iron Commissioner Cui Qiong memorialized to add reward, and he was ordered to act as Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and Iron Commissioner Cui Qiong memorialized recommending additional reward, and Yao was ordered to serve as acting Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 制出，令勖上省。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, Xu was ordered to enter the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, Yao was ordered to take up his post in the inner offices.

sentences.zh: 溫執奏曰：「國朝已來，郎官最為清選，不可以賞能吏。

translations.literal: Wen held fast and memorialized, saying, "Since the founding of the dynasty, bureau director posts have been the most select appointments—they cannot be used to reward capable clerks."
translations.idiomatic: Wen held firm and memorialized: "Since the founding of our dynasty, bureau director posts have been the most select appointments—they cannot be used to reward capable clerks."

sentences.zh: 」上令中使宣諭，言勖能官，且放入省。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered a eunuch commissioner to announce the imperial will, saying Xu was a capable official and should for the time being be allowed into the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent a eunuch commissioner to announce that Yao was a capable official and should for the time being be allowed into the inner offices.

sentences.zh: 溫堅執不奉詔，乃改勖檢校禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Wen firmly refused to obey the edict and had Xu changed to Acting Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wen firmly refused to obey and had Yao's appointment changed to Acting Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝謂楊嗣復曰：「韋溫不放姚勖入省，有故事否？

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to Yang Sifu, "Wei Wen would not let Yao Xu enter the inner offices—is there precedent for this?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to Yang Sifu, "Wei Wen would not let Yao Xu into the inner offices—is there precedent for this?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣復對曰：「韋溫誌在銓擇清流。

translations.literal: " Sifu replied, "Wei Wen's aim is to select and choose the pure stream."
translations.idiomatic: " Sifu replied, "Wei Wen aims to select only men of the pure stream."

sentences.zh: 然姚勖士行無玷，梁公元崇之孫，自殿中判鹽鐵案，陛下獎之，宜也。

translations.literal: Yet Yao Xu's conduct as a gentleman is without stain; he is grandson of Liang-dynasty Yuan Chong. From his post in the Palace Secretariat he judged Salt and Iron cases, and Your Majesty rewarded him—this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yao Xu's conduct is without stain—he is the grandson of Liang-dynasty Yuan Chong. From his post in the Palace Secretariat he handled Salt and Iron cases, and Your Majesty rewarded him, as was fitting.

sentences.zh: 若人有吏能，不入清流，孰為陛下當煩劇者？

translations.literal: If men of administrative ability do not enter the pure stream, who will undertake arduous duties for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If men of administrative ability cannot enter the pure stream, who will undertake arduous duties for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 此衰晉之風也。

translations.literal: This is the wind of decadent Jin.
translations.idiomatic: This is the spirit of decadent Jin.

sentences.zh: 」上素重溫，亦不奪其操，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: " The emperor had always valued Wen and did not override his principles, but sent him out as Military Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had always valued Wen and did not override his principles, but sent him out as Military Commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，李德裕用事，召拜吏部侍郎，欲引以為相。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held power; Wen was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, with the intention of making him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held power. Wen was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, with the intention of making him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時李漢以家行不謹，貶汾州司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Li Han, for misconduct in family affairs, was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Han had been demoted to Vice-Prefect of Fenzhou for misconduct in family affairs.

sentences.zh: 溫從容白德裕曰：「李漢不為相公所知，昨以不孝之罪絀免，乞加按問。

translations.literal: Wen calmly informed Deyu, saying, "Li Han is not known to the Chief Minister; yesterday he was dismissed for the crime of unfilial conduct—I beg that the case be reinvestigated."
translations.idiomatic: Wen calmly told Deyu, "Li Han is not known to you, Chief Minister. He was just dismissed on a charge of unfilial conduct—I beg that the case be reinvestigated."

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「親情耶？

translations.literal: " Deyu said, "A family connection?"
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu asked, "Is he a relative?"

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「雖非親昵，久相知耳。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "Though not a close relation, I have long known him."
translations.idiomatic: " Wen replied, "He is not a close relation, but I have known him for a long time."

sentences.zh: 」德裕不悅。

translations.literal: " Deyu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 居無何，出溫為宣歙觀察使，辟鄭處誨為觀察判官，德裕愈不悅。

translations.literal: Before long Wen was sent out as Military Commissioner of Xuan-She; he recruited Zheng Chuhui as administrative aide, and Deyu was still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wen was sent out as Military Commissioner of Xuan-She. He recruited Zheng Chuhui as his administrative aide, and Deyu was still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 池州人訟郡守，溫按之無狀，杖殺之。

translations.literal: A man of Chizhou sued the prefect; Wen investigated and found no substance, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Chizhou sued the prefect. Wen investigated and found no substance to the case, and had the plaintiff beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 明年，瘍生於首，謂愛婿張復魯曰：「予任校書郎時，夢二黃衣人賫符來追，及浐，將渡，一人續至曰：『彼墳至大，功須萬日。

translations.literal: The next year a carbuncle grew on his head; he said to his beloved son-in-law Zhang Fulü, "When I served as Proofreader I dreamed that two men in yellow robes bearing tally-sticks came to pursue me; reaching Chan, as I was about to cross, one who followed said, 'That tomb is very great—the merit requires ten thousand days.'"
translations.idiomatic: The next year a carbuncle grew on his head. He said to his beloved son-in-law Zhang Fulü, "When I served as Proofreader I dreamed that two men in yellow robes bearing tally-sticks came to pursue me. Reaching Chan, as I was about to cross, one who followed said, 'That tomb is very great—the merit requires ten thousand days.'"

sentences.zh: 』遂不涉而寤。

translations.literal: '" He did not cross and awoke.
translations.idiomatic: '" I did not cross and awoke.

sentences.zh: 計今萬日矣，與公訣矣。

translations.literal: I calculate that ten thousand days have now passed—I take leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: I calculate that ten thousand days have now passed—it is time to bid you farewell.

sentences.zh: 」明日卒，贈工部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: " The next day he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he died. He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 溫在朝時，與李玨、楊嗣復周旋。

translations.literal: When Wen was at court he associated with Li Jue and Yang Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: While Wen was at court he associated closely with Li Jue and Yang Sifu.

sentences.zh: 及楊、李禍作，嘆曰：「楊三、李七若取我語，豈至是耶！

translations.literal: When the Yang and Li calamity occurred, he sighed and said, "If Yang the Third and Li the Seventh had taken my words, how could it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: When the disasters befell Yang and Li, he sighed and said, "If Yang the Third and Li the Seventh had taken my advice, how could it have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」初溫以楊、李與德裕交怨，及居位，溫勸楊、李征用德裕，釋憾解慍。

translations.literal: " Earlier Wen, because Yang and Li were at odds with Deyu, when they took office urged Yang and Li to employ Deyu and release resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, because Yang and Li were at odds with Deyu, Wen had urged them when they took office to employ Deyu and lay aside their resentment.

sentences.zh: 二人不能用，故及禍。

translations.literal: The two could not use this counsel, and therefore met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The two would not follow his advice, and therefore met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 溫無子，女適薛蒙，善著文，續曹大家《女訓》十二章，士族傳寫，行於時。

translations.literal: Wen had no sons; his daughter married Xue Meng, who was skilled at writing and continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women in twelve chapters, which the gentry copied and circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had no sons. His daughter married Xue Meng, who was skilled at writing and continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women in twelve chapters, which the gentry copied and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 溫剛腸寡合，人多疏簡，唯與常侍蕭祐善。

translations.literal: Wen was stiff-spirited and rarely in accord; many kept him at a distance, and only with Regular Attendant Xiao You was he close.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was stiff-spirited and made few close friends; most kept their distance, and only Regular Attendant Xiao You was truly close to him.

sentences.zh: 附 蕭祐蕭祐者，蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Xiao You. Xiao You was a native of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Xiao You. Xiao You came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was orphaned and poor.

sentences.zh: 耿介苦學，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Upright and austere, he studied hard and was known for filial service to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and austere, he studied diligently and was known for filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 自處士征拜左拾遺，累遷至考功郎中。

translations.literal: From Recluse he was summoned and appointed Left Remembrancer, and was promoted in succession to Director in the merit section.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from private life, he was appointed Left Remembrancer and rose in succession to Director in the merit section.

sentences.zh: 祐博雅好古，尤喜圖畫。

translations.literal: You was broadly learned, fond of antiquity, and especially loved paintings.
translations.idiomatic: You was broadly learned and fond of antiquity, and especially loved paintings.

sentences.zh: 前代鐘、王遺法，蕭、張筆勢，編序真偽，為二十卷，元和末進禦，優詔嘉之，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: The surviving methods of Zhong and Wang of former ages, the brush manner of Xiao and Zhang—he arranged and distinguished true from false in twenty fascicles; at the end of Yuanhe he presented them to the throne, received an excellent edict of praise, and was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and distinguished authentic from spurious works among the surviving methods of Zhong and Wang and the brush manner of Xiao and Zhang into twenty fascicles. At the end of the Yuanhe era he presented them to the throne, received an edict of high praise, and was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 出為虢州刺史，入為太常少卿，轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Guo, entered as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was transferred to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Prefect of Guo, recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 逾月為桂州刺史、御史中丞、桂管防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: After more than a month he became Prefect of Gui, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Gui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was appointed Prefect of Gui, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Gui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太和二年八月，卒於官，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taihe he died in office and was posthumously made Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of the Taihe era he died in office and was posthumously made Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 祐閑淡貞退，善鼓琴賦詩，書畫盡妙。

translations.literal: You was leisurely, plain, upright, and retiring; skilled at playing the zither and composing poetry, his calligraphy and painting were all exquisite.
translations.idiomatic: You was leisurely, plain, upright, and retiring. He was skilled at playing the zither and composing poetry, and his calligraphy and painting were all exquisite.

sentences.zh: 遊心林壑，嘯詠終日，而名人高士，多與之遊。

translations.literal: His mind roamed in forests and ravines; he whistled and chanted all day, and famous men and lofty scholars mostly associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: His mind roamed among forests and ravines; he whistled and chanted poetry all day long, and many famous men and lofty scholars associated with him.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋溫尤重之，結為林泉之友。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Wen especially valued him and formed with him a friendship of forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wei Wen especially valued him, and they became close friends in retirement.

sentences.zh: =獨孤郁=

translations.literal: =Dugu Yu=
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yu

sentences.zh: 獨孤郁，河南人。

translations.literal: Dugu Yu was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yu came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 父及，天寶末與李華、蕭潁士等齊名。

translations.literal: His father Ji was in the late Tianbao era equal in fame to Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was, in the late Tianbao era, as famous as Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, and others.

sentences.zh: 善為文，所著《仙掌銘》，大為時流所賞，位終常州刺史。

translations.literal: Skilled at writing, his composition Inscription on the Immortal's Palm was greatly admired by men of the age; he ended his career as Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at writing. His Inscription on the Immortal's Palm was greatly admired by men of the age, and he ended his career as Prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 郁，貞元十四年登進士第，文學有父風，尤為舍人權德輿所稱，以子妻之。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan; in literary accomplishment he had his father's manner and was especially praised by Attendant Quan Deyu, who gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan. In literary accomplishment he had his father's manner and was especially praised by Attendant Quan Deyu, who gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he was Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he served as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和初，應制舉才識兼茂、明於體用，策入第四等，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe era he entered the special examination for talent and insight combined with excellence and clarity in substance and function; his policy essay ranked fourth class and he was appointed Left Remembrancer.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era he entered the special examination for talent and insight combined with excellence and clarity in substance and function. His policy essay ranked fourth class, and he was appointed Left Remembrancer.

sentences.zh: 太子司議郎杜從郁拜左補闕，郁與同列，論之曰：「從郁是宰臣佑之子，父居宰執，從郁不宜居諫列。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Admonisher Du Congyu was appointed Left Supplementation Censor; Yu and his colleagues discussed it, saying, "Congyu is the son of Chief Minister You; his father holds the chief ministership—Congyu ought not to hold a remonstrance post."
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Admonisher Du Congyu was appointed Left Supplementation Censor. Yu and his colleagues argued, "Congyu is the son of Chief Minister Du You. With his father holding the chief ministership, Congyu ought not to hold a remonstrance post."

sentences.zh: 」乃改為左拾遺，又論曰：「補闕之與拾遺，資品雖殊，同是諫官，若時政或有得失，不可令子論父。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon changed to Left Remembrancer, and they argued again, saying, "Supplementation Censor and Remembrancer differ in rank and grade, but both are remonstrance officials—if current policy has gains or losses, a son cannot be allowed to discuss his father."
translations.idiomatic: " He was thereupon changed to Left Remembrancer, and they argued again: "Supplementation Censor and Remembrancer differ in rank, but both are remonstrance officials. If current policy has gains or losses, a son cannot be allowed to remonstrate about his father."

sentences.zh: 」從郁竟改他官。

translations.literal: " Congyu was finally transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: " Congyu was finally transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉右補闕，又與同列拜章論中官吐突承璀不宜為河北招討使，乃改招撫宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor; again with his colleagues he submitted a memorial arguing that the eunuch Tutu Chenghui ought not to be Hebei Campaign Commissioner, and Chenghui was changed to Pacification and Comfort Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor. Again with his colleagues he submitted a memorial arguing that the eunuch Tutu Chenghui ought not to be Hebei Campaign Commissioner, and Chenghui was changed to Pacification and Comfort Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was additionally made Compiler at the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was additionally appointed Compiler at the History Office.

sentences.zh: 尋召充翰林學士，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and promoted to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 權德輿作相，郁以婦公辭內職。

translations.literal: When Quan Deyu became chief minister, Yu declined the inner post because of his father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Deyu became chief minister, Yu declined the inner post because of his relationship as son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 憲宗曰：「德輿乃有此佳婿。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong said, "Deyu has such a fine son-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong said, "Deyu has such a fine son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 」因詔宰相於士族之家，選尚公主者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the chief ministers to select from gentry families those to marry princesses.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he ordered the chief ministers to select men from gentry families to marry princesses.

sentences.zh: 遷郁考功員外郎，充史館修撰、判館事，預修《德宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Yu was promoted to Vice Director in the merit section and appointed Compiler at the History Office with charge of office affairs, participating in the compilation of Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was promoted to Vice Director in the merit section and appointed Compiler at the History Office with charge of office affairs, participating in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 七年，以本官復知制誥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, retaining his original post, he again served as Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while retaining his original post, he again served as Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉駕部郎中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Transport.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，復召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was again summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he was again summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 九年，以疾辭內職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on grounds of illness, he resigned the inner post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he resigned the inner post on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十一月，改秘書少監，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 弟 朗郁弟朗，嘗居諫官，請罷淮西用兵，不協旨，貶興元戶曹。

translations.literal: Younger brother Lang. Yu's younger brother Lang had once held a remonstrance post; he requested cessation of military action in Huaixi, failed to accord with the imperial will, and was demoted to Registrar of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Lang. Yu's younger brother Lang had once served as a remonstrance official. He requested cessation of military action in Huaixi, failed to accord with the imperial will, and was demoted to Registrar of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，轉殿中。

translations.literal: He entered as Investigating Censor and was transferred to the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Investigating Censor and transferred to the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十五年，兼充史館修撰，遷都官員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was additionally made Compiler at the History Office and promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was additionally appointed Compiler at the History Office and promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Justice.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，諫議大夫李景儉於史館飲酒，憑醉謁宰相，語辭侵侮；

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era Remonstrating Grand Master Li Jingjian drank at the History Office and, relying on drunkenness, called on the chief minister with insulting words;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Changqing era Remonstrating Grand Master Li Jingjian drank at the History Office and, while drunk, called on the chief minister with insulting words;

sentences.zh: 朗坐同飲，出為漳州刺史。

translations.literal: Lang was punished for drinking together and was sent out as Prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was punished for drinking together with him and was sent out as Prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為左司員外郎，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Director in the Left Bureau and was promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Director in the Left Bureau and promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 揚州節度使王播罷兼鹽鐵使，行賂於中人，求復領銅鹽。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Military Commissioner Wang Bo had been removed from his concurrent post as Salt and Iron Commissioner; he offered bribes to inner attendants seeking to resume charge of copper and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou Military Commissioner Wang Bo had been removed from his concurrent post as Salt and Iron Commissioner. He offered bribes to inner attendants seeking to resume charge of copper and salt.

sentences.zh: 朗上章論之。

translations.literal: Lang submitted a memorial arguing against this.
translations.idiomatic: Lang submitted a memorial arguing against this.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年十一月，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of the Baoli era he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year he was granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year he was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李道樞乘醉謁朗；

translations.literal: Attending Censor Li Daoshu, relying on drunkenness, called on Lang;
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Li Daoshu, while drunk, called on Lang;

sentences.zh: 朗劾之，左授司議郎。

translations.literal: Lang impeached him and had him demoted to the left as Admonisher.
translations.idiomatic: Lang impeached him and had him demoted to Admonisher.

sentences.zh: 憲府故事，三院御史由大夫、中丞自辟，請命於朝。

translations.literal: By censorate precedent, censors of the three bureaus were recruited by the chief censor or vice chief censor and then requested appointment from the court.
translations.idiomatic: By censorate precedent, censors of the three bureaus were recruited by the chief censor or vice chief censor and then requested appointment from the court.

sentences.zh: 時崔晃、鄭居中不由憲長而除，皆丞相之僚舊也，敕命雖行，朗拒而不納，晃竟改太常博士，居中分司東臺。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Huang and Zheng Juzhong were appointed without going through the censorate chief—both were old associates of the chief minister; though the edict was issued, Lang refused to accept them; Huang was finally changed to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Juzhong was assigned to the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Huang and Zheng Juzhong were appointed without going through the censorate chief—both were old associates of the chief minister. Though the edict was issued, Lang refused to accept them. Huang was finally changed to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Juzhong was assigned to the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，高少逸入閣失儀，朗不彈奏，宰相銜阻崔晃事，左授少逸贊善大夫，朗亦罰俸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Gao Shaoyi entered the gate with breach of ritual; Lang did not impeach him; the chief minister, bearing a grudge over the Cui Huang affair, demoted Shaoyi to Supplementation Grand Master and Lang also had his salary penalized.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Gao Shaoyi entered the gate with breach of ritual. Lang did not impeach him. The chief minister, bearing a grudge over the Cui Huang affair, demoted Shaoyi to Supplementation Grand Master and penalized Lang's salary as well.

sentences.zh: 朗稱執法不稱，乞罷中丞，敬宗令中使諭之，不允其讓。

translations.literal: Lang said his enforcement of the law was unworthy and begged to be removed as vice chief censor; Emperor Jingzong ordered a eunuch commissioner to instruct him and did not grant his resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Lang said his enforcement of the law was unworthy and begged to be removed as vice chief censor. Emperor Jingzong sent a eunuch commissioner to instruct him and did not grant his resignation.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was changed to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太和元年八月，出為福州刺史、御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Taihe he was sent out as Prefect of Fuzhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of the Taihe era he was sent out as Prefect of Fuzhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 是月赴官，暴卒於路，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: That month he went to take up his post and died suddenly on the road; he was posthumously made Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: That month he set out to take up his post and died suddenly on the road. He was posthumously made Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子 庠郁子庠，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: Son Xiang. Yu's son Xiang also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiang. Yu's son Xiang also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中後官達，亦至侍郎。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong era he reached high office and also attained Vice Minister rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era he reached high office and also attained the rank of Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: =錢徽=

translations.literal: =Qian Hui=
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hui

sentences.zh: 錢徽，字蔚章，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Qian Hui, styled Weizhang, was a native of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hui, courtesy name Weizhang, came from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父起，天寶十年登進士第。

translations.literal: His father Qi passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 起能五言詩。

translations.literal: Qi was skilled at five-character poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was skilled at five-character poetry.

sentences.zh: 初從鄉薦，寄家江湖，嘗於客舍月夜獨吟，遽聞人吟於庭曰：「曲終人不見，江上數峰青。

translations.literal: When he first received recommendation from his district, his family lodged on the rivers and lakes; once in a moonlit night at an inn he chanted alone and suddenly heard someone chanting in the courtyard, saying, "The tune ends and the man is not seen—on the river, several peaks are green."
translations.idiomatic: When he first received recommendation from his district, his family lodged on the rivers and lakes. Once on a moonlit night at an inn he chanted alone and suddenly heard someone chanting in the courtyard: "The tune ends and the man is not seen—on the river, several peaks are green."

sentences.zh: 」起愕然，攝衣視之，無所見矣，以為鬼怪，而誌其一十字。

translations.literal: " Qi was startled, straightened his robes and looked—nothing was seen; he thought it a ghost and recorded the ten characters.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi was startled, straightened his robes and looked, but saw nothing. He thought it a ghost and recorded the ten characters.

sentences.zh: 起就試之年，李暐所試《湘靈鼓瑟詩》題中有「青」字，起即以鬼謠十字為落句，暐深嘉之，稱為絕唱。

translations.literal: In the year Qi took the examination, Li Wei set the topic Xiangling Plays the Zither, which contained the character "green"; Qi used the ghost's ten characters as his closing line; Wei greatly praised it and called it a supreme composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Qi took the examination, Li Wei set the topic Xiangling Plays the Zither, which contained the character for "green." Qi used the ghost's ten characters as his closing line. Wei greatly praised it and called it a supreme composition.

sentences.zh: 是歲登第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: That year he passed and on leaving the boll was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That year he passed and on completing his studies was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，與韓翃、李端輩十人，俱以能詩，出入貴遊之門，時號「十才子」，形於圖畫。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, with Han Hong, Li Duan, and nine others, all skilled at poetry, they moved in and out of the gates of noble pleasure-seekers; the age called them the Ten Talents, and they were depicted in paintings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, together with Han Hong, Li Duan, and nine others, all skilled at poetry, they moved in and out of the gates of noble pleasure-seekers. The age called them the Ten Talents, and they were depicted in paintings.

sentences.zh: 起位終尚書郎。

translations.literal: Qi ended his career as a Director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Qi ended his career as a Director in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 徽，貞元初進士擢第，從事戎幕。

translations.literal: Hui, in the early Zhenyuan era, passed the jinshi examination and served in military staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui passed the jinshi examination in the early Zhenyuan era and served in military staffs.

sentences.zh: 元和初入朝，三遷祠部員外郎，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Yuanhe began he entered court, was thrice promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanhe era began he entered court, was thrice promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉祠部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites and made Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites and made Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年，改司封郎中、賜緋魚袋，職如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was changed to Director in the Bureau of Seals and Grants and given the crimson fish bag; his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Seals and Grants and given the crimson fish bag; his duties remained as before.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王師討淮西，詔朝臣議兵，徽上疏言用兵累歲，供饋力殫，宜罷淮西之征。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the imperial army campaigned against Huaixi; the court ordered the assembled ministers to discuss military affairs; Hui submitted a memorial saying that troops had been used for successive years, supplies were exhausted, and the Huaixi campaign ought to be halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the imperial army campaigned against Huaixi. The court ordered the assembled ministers to discuss military affairs. Hui submitted a memorial saying that troops had been used for successive years, supplies were exhausted, and the Huaixi campaign ought to be halted.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不悅，罷徽學士之職，守本官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was displeased, removed Hui from his academicianship, and kept him at his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was displeased, removed Hui from his academicianship, and kept him at his original post.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he was Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing he was Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時宰相段文昌出鎮蜀川。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Duan Wenchang went out to command Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Minister Duan Wenchang was posted to command Shu.

sentences.zh: 文昌好學，尤喜圖書古畫。

translations.literal: Wenchang loved learning and especially loved books, paintings, and antiquities.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang loved learning and especially loved books, paintings, and antiquities.

sentences.zh: 故刑部侍郎楊憑兄弟，以文學知名，家多書畫，鐘、王、張、鄭之跡在《書斷》、《畫呂》者，兼而有之。

translations.literal: The brothers Yang Ping, former Vice Minister of Justice, were known for literary accomplishment; their household had many books and paintings—traces of Zhong, Wang, Zhang, and Zheng recorded in Judgment on Calligraphy and Record of Painting, they possessed together.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Yang Ping, former Vice Minister of Justice, were known for literary accomplishment. Their household possessed many books and paintings, including works by Zhong, Wang, Zhang, and Zheng recorded in Judgment on Calligraphy and Record of Painting.

sentences.zh: 憑子渾之求進，盡以家藏書畫獻文昌，求致進士第。

translations.literal: Ping's son Hunzhi sought advancement and presented all the family's collected books and paintings to Wenchang, seeking to obtain a jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son Hunzhi sought advancement and presented all the family's collected books and paintings to Wenchang, seeking to obtain a jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 文昌將發，面托錢徽，繼以私書保薦。

translations.literal: When Wenchang was about to depart, he entrusted Hui in person and followed with a private letter recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenchang was about to depart, he entrusted Hui in person and followed with a private letter recommending Hunzhi.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李紳亦托舉子周漢賓於徽。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Shen also entrusted his examination candidate Zhou Hanbin to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Shen also entrusted his examination candidate Zhou Hanbin to Hui.

sentences.zh: 及榜出，渾之、漢賓皆不中選。

translations.literal: When the list was issued, neither Hunzhi nor Hanbin was selected.
translations.idiomatic: When the list was issued, neither Hunzhi nor Hanbin was selected.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔與元稹素相厚善。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin and Yuan Zhen had long been thick friends.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin and Yuan Zhen had long been close friends.

sentences.zh: 初稹以直道譴逐久之，及得還朝，大改前志。

translations.literal: At first Zhen, because of the straight path, was censured and banished for a long time; when he was able to return to court, he greatly changed his former resolve.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhen, because of his upright conduct, had been censured and banished for a long time. When he was able to return to court, he greatly changed his former resolve.

sentences.zh: 由逕以僥進達，宗閔亦急於進取，二人遂有嫌隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced through opportunism; Zongmin also was eager for advancement, and the two came to have mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he advanced through opportunism. Zongmin also was eager for advancement, and the two came to bear mutual resentment.

sentences.zh: 楊汝士與徽有舊。

translations.literal: Yang Rushi and Hui had an old association.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rushi and Hui had an old association.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宗閔子婿蘇巢及汝士季弟殷士俱及第。

translations.literal: That year Zongmin's son-in-law Su Chao and Rushi's youngest brother Yinshi both passed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zongmin's son-in-law Su Chao and Rushi's youngest brother Yinshi both passed the examination.

sentences.zh: 故文昌、李紳大怒。

translations.literal: Therefore Wenchang and Li Shen were greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wenchang and Li Shen were greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 文昌赴鎮。

translations.literal: Wenchang went to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang departed for his command.

sentences.zh: 辭日，內殿面奏，言徽所放進士鄭朗等十四人，皆子弟藝薄，不當在選中。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he reported in the inner hall that the jinshi Hui had passed—Zheng Lang and fourteen others—were all sons of officials with thin accomplishment and ought not to have been selected.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his farewell audience he reported in the inner hall that the jinshi Hui had passed—Zheng Lang and fourteen others—were all sons of officials with thin accomplishment and ought not to have been selected.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以其事訪於學士元稹、李紳，二人對與文昌同。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong inquired about the matter of the Academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen; the two answered in accord with Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong inquired about the matter of the Academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen; the two answered in accord with Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 遂命中書舍人王起、主客郎中知制誥白居易，於子亭重試，內出題目《孤竹管賦》、《鳥散余花落》詩，而十人不中選。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Secretariat Drafter Wang Qi and Director in the Bureau of Guests Bai Juyi, who also served as Drafting Secretary, to conduct a re-examination at the Ziting; topics issued from within were the rhapsody Guzhu Pipes and the poem Birds Scatter, Flowers Yet Fall, and ten men were not selected.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Secretariat Drafter Wang Qi and Director in the Bureau of Guests Bai Juyi, who also served as Drafting Secretary, to conduct a re-examination at the Ziting. Topics issued from within were the rhapsody Guzhu Pipes and the poem Birds Scatter, Flowers Yet Fall, and ten men failed to pass.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict said:

sentences.zh: 國家設文學之科，本求才實，茍容僥幸，則異至公。

translations.literal: The state establishes the literary examination to seek real talent; if it tolerates opportunism, it differs from utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The state establishes the literary examination to seek real talent. If it tolerates opportunism, it falls short of utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 訪聞近日浮薄之徒，扇為朋黨，謂之關節，幹撓主司。

translations.literal: It has been learned that recently shallow men fan factional ties, called "gate connections," and interfere with the chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: It has been learned that recently shallow men have formed factional ties, called "gate connections," and have interfered with the chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 每歲策名，無不先定，永言敗俗，深用興懷。

translations.literal: Each year the registered names are all predetermined beforehand—ever speaking of corrupting custom, I am deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the successful candidates are all predetermined beforehand. Speaking of the corruption of custom, I am deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 鄭朗等昨令重試，意在精核藝能，不於異書之中，固求深僻題目，責令所試成就，以觀學藝淺深。

translations.literal: Zheng Lang and the others were yesterday ordered to re-examine; the intent was to scrutinize artistic ability—not to seek abstruse topics from strange books, but to charge them to complete what was tested and observe the depth or shallowness of their learning and art.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lang and the others were ordered to re-examine yesterday. The intent was to scrutinize their artistic ability—not to seek abstruse topics from strange books, but to require them to complete what was tested and observe the depth or shallowness of their learning.

sentences.zh: 孤竹管是祭天之樂，出於《周禮》正經；

translations.literal: Guzhu pipes are music for sacrificing to Heaven, coming from the orthodox classic Rites of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Guzhu pipes are music for sacrificing to Heaven, coming from the orthodox classic Rites of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 閱其呈試之文，都不知其本事，辭律鄙淺，蕪累亦多。

translations.literal: reading their submitted examination compositions, they did not know the basic matter at all; diction and rules were vulgar and shallow, and redundancy was also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Reading their submitted examination compositions, they did not know the basic matter at all. Their diction and prosody were vulgar and shallow, and their work was also abundantly redundant.

sentences.zh: 比令宣示錢徽，庶其深自懷愧，誠宜盡棄，以警將來。

translations.literal: It was recently ordered to show this to Qian Hui, hoping he would deeply feel shame; they truly ought all to be rejected to warn the future.
translations.idiomatic: This was shown to Qian Hui, hoping he would deeply feel shame. They truly ought all to be rejected to warn the future.

sentences.zh: 但以四海無虞，人心方泰，用弘寧撫，式示殊恩，特掩爾瑕，庶明予誌。

translations.literal: But because within the four seas there is no worry and people's hearts are at peace, employing broad pacification and showing special grace, I specially cover your flaws, hoping to make clear my intent.
translations.idiomatic: But because within the four seas there is no worry and people's hearts are at peace, employing broad pacification and showing special grace, I specially cover your flaws, hoping to make clear my intent.

sentences.zh: 孔溫業、趙存約、竇洵直所試粗通，與及第；

translations.literal: Kong Wenye, Zhao Cunyue, and Dou Xunzhi were roughly competent in what was tested and were given passing grades;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenye, Zhao Cunyue, and Dou Xunzhi were roughly competent in what was tested and were given passing grades;

sentences.zh: 裴撰特賜及第；

translations.literal: Pei Zhuan was specially granted passing grade;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhuan was specially granted a passing grade;

sentences.zh: 鄭朗等十人並落下。

translations.literal: Zheng Lang and ten others were all struck from the list.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lang and ten others were all struck from the list.

sentences.zh: 自今後禮部舉人，宜準開元二十五年敕，及第訖，所試雜文並策，送中書門下詳覆。

translations.literal: From now on candidates of the Ministry of Rites ought to follow the edict of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan: when passing is complete, the miscellaneous compositions and policy essays tested shall be sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: From now on candidates of the Ministry of Rites ought to follow the edict of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan: when the examination is complete, the miscellaneous compositions and policy essays tested shall be sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 尋貶徽為江州刺史，中書舍人李宗閔劍州刺史，右補闕楊汝士開江令。

translations.literal: Soon Hui was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou, Secretariat Drafter Li Zongmin to Prefect of Jianzhou, and Right Supplementation Censor Yang Rushi to Magistrate of Kaijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hui was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou, Secretariat Drafter Li Zongmin to Prefect of Jianzhou, and Right Supplementation Censor Yang Rushi to Magistrate of Kaijiang.

sentences.zh: 初議貶徽，宗閔、汝士令徽以文昌、李紳私書進呈，上必開悟。

translations.literal: When demotion of Hui was first discussed, Zongmin and Rushi had Hui present Wenchang's and Li Shen's private letters to the throne—the emperor would surely be enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: When demotion of Hui was first discussed, Zongmin and Rushi urged Hui to present Wenchang's and Li Shen's private letters to the throne—the emperor would surely be enlightened.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 茍無愧心，得喪一致，修身慎行，安可以私書相證耶？

translations.literal: If one has no guilty conscience, gain and loss are alike; by cultivating the self and acting with caution—how can one use private letters as evidence?
translations.idiomatic: If one's conscience is clear, gain and loss are alike. By cultivating oneself and acting with care, how can one use private letters as evidence?

sentences.zh: 」令子弟焚之，人士稱徽長者。

translations.literal: " He ordered his sons and younger relatives to burn them; men of society praised Hui as a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " He had his sons and younger relatives burn them, and men of society praised Hui as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 既而穆宗知其朋比之端，乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: Soon afterward Muzong learned of the signs of their factional collusion, and issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long Muzong learned of their factional collusion and issued an edict saying:

sentences.zh: 昔者，卿大夫相與讓於朝，士庶人相與讓於列；

translations.literal: In antiquity, ministers and grandees yielded to one another in court, and scholars and common people yielded to one another in their ranks;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, ministers and grandees yielded to one another at court, and scholars and commoners yielded to one another in their ranks;

sentences.zh: 周成王刑措不用，漢文帝恥言人過，真理古也，朕甚慕焉。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Zhou put punishments aside and did not use them; Emperor Wen of Han was ashamed to speak of others' faults—truly reason lies in antiquity, and I greatly admire this.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou set punishments aside and did not use them; Emperor Wen of Han was ashamed to speak of others' faults. Truth indeed lies in antiquity, and I greatly admire this.

sentences.zh: 中代已還，爭端斯起，掩抑其言則專蔽，誘掖其說則侵誣。

translations.literal: From the middle ages onward, disputes arose; suppressing speech leads to monopoly and concealment, while drawing out and encouraging talk leads to infringement and false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: From the middle ages onward, disputes arose. Suppress speech and one becomes monopolistic and secretive; encourage and draw out talk and one invites slander and false accusation.

sentences.zh: 自非責實循名，不能彰善癉惡，故孝宣必有告訐及下，光武不以單辭遽行。

translations.literal: Unless one demands facts and follows names, one cannot display good and conceal evil; thus Emperor Xuan always had informants reaching down, and Emperor Guangwu did not act hastily on a single statement.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one demands facts and follows names, one cannot reward good and punish evil. Thus Emperor Xuan always required informants to reach down, and Emperor Guangwu did not act hastily on a single accusation.

sentences.zh: 《語》稱訕上之非，律有匿名之禁，皆以防三至之毀，重兩造之明。

translations.literal: The Analects speaks against slandering one's superiors; the law has a prohibition on anonymous accusations—all to guard against thrice-repeated slander and to emphasize clarity for both parties.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects condemns slandering one's superiors, and the law forbids anonymous accusations—all to guard against rumor thrice repeated and to ensure clarity for both sides.

sentences.zh: 是以爵人於朝則皆勸，刑人於市則皆懼，罪有歸而賞當事也。

translations.literal: Thus when ennobling a man in court all are encouraged, when punishing a man in the marketplace all are in fear—crime has its attribution and rewards match the deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a man is ennobled at court, all are encouraged; when a man is punished in the marketplace, all are in fear. Crime has its proper attribution, and rewards match the deeds.

sentences.zh: 末代偷巧，內荏外剛。

translations.literal: In the last age men are shrewd and crafty—soft within, hard without.
translations.idiomatic: In the final age men grew shrewd and crafty—soft within and hard without.

sentences.zh: 卿大夫無進思盡忠之誠，多退有後言之謗；

translations.literal: Ministers and grandees lack the sincerity of advancing with loyal thoughts; when withdrawn, many have slander spoken afterward;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and grandees lack the sincerity to advance with loyal counsel; once withdrawn, many speak slander behind one's back;

sentences.zh: 士庶人無切磋琢磨之益，多鑠浸潤之讒。

translations.literal: Scholars and common people lack the benefit of mutual polishing; many have slander that seeps and saturates.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners lack the benefit of mutual refinement; many suffer slander that seeps in and saturates.

sentences.zh: 進則諛言諂笑以相求，退則群居州處以相議。

translations.literal: When advancing they use flattering words and servile smiles to seek from one another; when withdrawn they gather in groups and dwell together to discuss one another.
translations.idiomatic: In office they use flattery and servile smiles to seek favor from one another; out of office they gather in groups and dwell together to gossip about one another.

sentences.zh: 留中不出之請，蓋發其陰私；

translations.literal: Requests held within and not issued largely expose private secrets;
translations.idiomatic: Memorials held within and not issued largely serve to expose private secrets;

sentences.zh: 公論不容之誅，是生於朋黨。

translations.literal: Punishment intolerable to public opinion arises from factional cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments that public opinion cannot tolerate arise from factional cliques.

sentences.zh: 擢一官，則曰恩皆自我；

translations.literal: Promote one office, and they say the favor all comes from oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Promote one man to office, and they say the favor all came from themselves;

sentences.zh: 黜一職，則曰事出他門。

translations.literal: Dismiss one post, and they say the matter came from another faction.
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss one man from office, and they say the matter came from another faction.

sentences.zh: 比周之跡已彰，尚矜介特；

translations.literal: Evidence of banding together is already clear, yet they still pride themselves on exceptional integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Evidence of factional collusion is already plain, yet they still pride themselves on exceptional integrity;

sentences.zh: 由徑之蹤盡露，自謂貞方。

translations.literal: Tracks of taking shortcuts are fully exposed, yet they call themselves upright and proper.
translations.idiomatic: Tracks of taking shortcuts are fully exposed, yet they call themselves upright and proper.

sentences.zh: 居省寺者不以勤恪蒞官，而曰務從簡易；

translations.literal: Those dwelling in ministries and courts do not attend to office with diligence and reverence, but say they aim for simplicity and ease;
translations.idiomatic: Those in the ministries and courts do not attend to office with diligence and reverence, but say they aim for simplicity and ease;

sentences.zh: 提紀綱者不以準繩檢下，而曰密奏風聞。

translations.literal: Those who hold the reins of law do not examine subordinates by standards and measure, but say they secretly memorialize on hearsay.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold the reins of law do not examine subordinates by rule and measure, but say they secretly memorialize on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 獻章疏者更相是非，備顧問者互有憎愛。

translations.literal: Those presenting memorials contradict one another back and forth; those serving as advisers mutually harbor likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submit memorials contradict one another; those who serve as advisers mutually harbor likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 茍非秦鏡照膽，堯羊觸邪，時君聽之，安可不惑？

translations.literal: If not for Qin's mirror that illuminates the heart and Yao's goat that butts the wicked, when the ruler of the age hears this, how could he not be confused?
translations.idiomatic: Without Qin's mirror that illuminates the heart and Yao's goat that butts the wicked, when the ruler of the age hears such things, how could he not be confused?

sentences.zh: 參斷一謬，俗化益訛。

translations.literal: One error in judgment, and custom and transformation grow ever more corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: One error in judgment, and custom and moral transformation grow ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 禍發齒牙，言生枝葉，率是道也，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: Disaster arises from teeth and tongue; words spawn branches and leaves—all follow this path, and I greatly pity it.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster arises from teeth and tongue; words spawn branches and leaves—all follow this path, and I am deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 我國家貞觀、開元，同符三代，風俗歸厚，禮讓皆行。

translations.literal: Our state's Zhenguan and Kaiyuan matched the Three Dynasties; custom returned to thickness, courtesy and yielding were all practiced.
translations.idiomatic: In our state's Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, we matched the Three Dynasties; custom returned to earnestness, and courtesy and yielding were fully practiced.

sentences.zh: 兵興已來，人散久矣。

translations.literal: Since warfare arose, the people have long been scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Since warfare arose, the people have long been scattered.

sentences.zh: 始欲導之以德，不欲驅之以刑。

translations.literal: At first we wished to guide them with virtue, not drive them with punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At first we wished to guide them with virtue, not drive them with punishments.

sentences.zh: 然而信有未孚，理有未至，曾無恥格，益用雕元刂。

translations.literal: Yet trust has not been fully realized, principle has not fully reached; there has never been shame sufficient to reform conduct, and harsh legal measures have increased all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet trust has not been fully realized and principle has not fully prevailed. Shame has never been sufficient to reform conduct, and harsh legal measures have been applied all the more.

sentences.zh: 小則綜核之權，見侵於下輩；

translations.literal: In small matters the power of comprehensive review is encroached upon by junior men;
translations.idiomatic: In small matters the power of comprehensive review is encroached upon by junior men;

sentences.zh: 大則樞機之重，旁撓於薄徒。

translations.literal: In great matters the weight of pivot and hinge is sidelined and interfered with by shallow fellows.
translations.idiomatic: In great matters the weight of state policy is sidelined and interfered with by shallow men.

sentences.zh: 尚念因而化之，亦冀去其尤者。

translations.literal: Still thinking to transform them thereby, also hoping to remove the worst among them.
translations.idiomatic: Still we hoped to transform them thereby and to remove the worst among them.

sentences.zh: 而宰臣懼其浸染，未克澄清。

translations.literal: But the chief ministers feared their spread and corruption, and could not achieve clarity.
translations.idiomatic: But the chief ministers feared their spread and corruption and could not achieve clarity.

sentences.zh: 備引祖宗之書，願垂勸誡之詔，遂伸告諭，頗用殷勤。

translations.literal: Fully citing the books of the ancestors, they wished to grant an edict of admonition and warning; thus they extended proclamation and instruction, with considerable earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Fully citing the books of the ancestors, they asked that an edict of admonition and warning be issued; thus they extended proclamation and instruction with considerable earnestness.

sentences.zh: 各當自省厥躬，與我同底於道。

translations.literal: Each ought to examine himself, and with me reach the same foundation in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you ought to examine yourselves and with me reach the same foundation in the Way.

sentences.zh: 元稹之辭也。

translations.literal: These were the words of Yuan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: These were the words of Yuan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 制出，朋比之徒，如撻於市，鹹睚眥於紳、稹。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the factional clique, as though flogged in the marketplace, all bore grudges against Shen and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the factionalists, as though publicly flogged, all bore grudges against Li Shen and Yuan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 徽明年遷華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍等使。

translations.literal: The next year Hui was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture, Defense Commissioner of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of Zhenguo Army and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hui was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture, Defense Commissioner of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and other posts.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，征拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Wenzong acceded, Hui was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong acceded, Hui was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太和元年十二月，復授華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taihe, he was again appointed Prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taihe, he was again appointed Prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，以疾辭位，授吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year, he resigned his post on grounds of illness and was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel with retirement status.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year, he resigned on grounds of illness and was granted the title Minister of the Ministry of Personnel with retirement status.

sentences.zh: 三年三月卒，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he died, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year he died, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子可復、可及，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Kefu and Keji both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kefu and Keji both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 可復累官至禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Kefu rose through successive offices to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Kefu rose through successive offices to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，鄭註出鎮鳳翔，李訓選名家子以為賓佐，授可復檢校兵部郎中、兼御史中丞，充鳳翔節度副使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, Zheng Zhu went out to command Fengxiang; Li Xun selected sons of eminent families to serve as staff and appointed Kefu Acting Director in the Ministry of War, also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and made him deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe, Zheng Zhu went out to command Fengxiang. Li Xun selected sons of eminent families to serve on his staff and appointed Kefu Acting Director in the Ministry of War, also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief, as deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，李訓敗，鄭註誅，可復為鳳翔監軍使所害。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, Li Xun was defeated and Zheng Zhu was executed; Kefu was killed by the Fengxiang army supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year, Li Xun was defeated and Zheng Zhu was executed. Kefu was killed by the Fengxiang army supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: =高釴=
